description: Tier 1 rule-based detection on CICFlowMeter flow records. Every threshold is here; change it here, not in code. Count thresholds are multiplied by the sensitivity factor (high sensitivity = lower thresholds = more alerts).

T1-PORTSCAN-01.description: One source probes many destination ports of one host inside a window, each probe carrying almost no data.

T1-DDOS-01.description: Several sources each flood the same destination service inside a window.
T1-DDOS-01.disabled_reason: No tested setting keeps benign false alarms at or below 1%: the best flags 6.71% of benign flows on held-out data (recall 0.8162, precision 0.5356). Enable only on a network whose busy services are known; the DoS rule still flags each flooding source individually.

T1-DOS-01.description: One source opens a sustained, high number of flows to one destination service inside a window. Name-service ports are excluded: many small queries to a resolver are normal, and DNS abuse is its own class.

T1-SLOWLORIS-01.description: One source holds many long, near-idle connections open to a web service at the same time.

T1-BRUTEFORCE-01.description: One source makes many connection attempts of similar size to an authentication service inside a window.

T1-C2-01.description: One source contacts the same destination service at regular intervals across the capture.

T1-EXFIL-01.description: A flow sends far more data out than it receives.

T1-DNS-01.description: Many DNS flows between one host and one resolver inside a window whose replies are many times the size of the queries (amplification / reflection).

T1-TLS-01.description: One source makes many short TLS connections that end in a reset inside a window: failed or aborted handshakes.

tuning.method: Thresholds chosen on flows in even-numbered minutes of TII-SSRC-23 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 (02-20-2018), tested on flows in odd-numbered minutes.
tuning.selection: best F1 on the rule's own class with benign false alarms <= 1%
tuning.untuned_reason: no labelled attack flows with real addresses and timestamps for these classes

allowlist.description: Known-good traffic: flows to or from these addresses, or to these destination ports, are marked Benign and no other rule is applied to them. Empty by default; fill in per network (resolvers, NTP, update servers, backup jobs).

packet_rules.description: Tier 2 header, ARP and unencrypted-payload checks, run with scapy on the uploaded pcap (packet_rule_service.py).

T2-MITM-01.description: Several MAC addresses claim one IP address in ARP replies, or a burst of gratuitous ARP.

T2-EVASION-01.description: Illegal TCP flag sets (NULL, XMAS, SYN+FIN), overlapping IP fragments, or TTL changes inside one flow.

T2-WEB-01.description: An unencrypted HTTP request line or body (URL-decoded) matches an injection pattern: SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, command injection. A fallback for when Suricata is not installed; Suricata's ET WEB_SERVER rules are the primary source.

T2-API-01.description: One source calls API paths at a high rate, or collects many 401 / 403 / 429 replies, inside a window.

T2-BRUTEFORCE-01.description: Failed-login replies to one client inside a window: FTP 530, SMTP 535, POP3 -ERR, HTTP 401.

T2-DNS-01.description: One client sends many DNS queries with long or random-looking names inside a window (tunnelling).

T2-TLS-01.description: A TLS ClientHello offers SSL 2.0, SSL 3.0 or TLS 1.0 as its highest version. The handshake is sent in the clear, so this works on encrypted traffic.

T2-BOF-01.description: An unencrypted payload carries a long NOP run (0x90) or a long run of one filler character, typical of an overflow payload.

suricata.description: Tier 2 signature engine: suricata -r <pcap> with the Emerging Threats Open ruleset. Used when the binary is found (FORENXAI_SURICATA, tools/suricata/, PATH, or C:/Program Files/Suricata); otherwise its classes rely on the scapy checks above and the case records that Suricata did not run.

categories: Detection of a Denial of Service Attack
Malware Command and Control Activity Detected

suricata.class_mapping_note: Ordered: the first entry whose signature prefix or category (Suricata's classtype description as written in eve.json) matches wins; 'contains' words, when given, must also appear in the signature. Unmapped signatures are listed in the case's rule_analysis.

decision.description: decide(): which detector's class becomes the verdict. trust = 'rule' only where the rule was measured as precise on held-out data (tuning.test_results precision >= 0.9); every other class trusts the model. Confidence thresholds and the out-of-distribution limit come from the model bundle (decision_thresholds.json, ood_stats.json).
